# Phase Two — Twenty Safety Improvements

1. Compare every branch against `origin/main`, not stale local `main`.
2. Count unique commits in both directions for every branch.
3. List exact unique commit subjects before merging.
4. Measure dirty state of every existing worktree separately.
5. Treat missing/prunable worktrees differently from live dirty worktrees.
6. Categorize canonical dirt by status code and top-level path.
7. Scan untracked candidates for secret-like filenames before staging.
8. Scan large untracked files before staging.
9. Do not stage `.env`, credentials, key material, node_modules, caches, logs, build archives, or tunnel state.
10. Make canonical local work durable on `main` before integrating remote history.
11. Avoid squash if history contains meaningful independent release commits unless conflict pressure demands it.
12. Prefer a normal merge of `origin/main` into canonical `main` so both histories survive.
13. For side branches already merged upstream, delete references without replaying commits.
14. For side branches with unique commits, inspect patch-id/content overlap before replay.
15. Harvest uncommitted worktree diffs before deleting worktrees.
16. Re-run `git branch --no-merged main` after every convergence wave.
17. Re-run worktree dirty checks before removals.
18. Push only after final branch/worktree uniqueness reaches zero or remaining items are explicitly proven junk.
19. Keep release/UI/workspace tests grouped so failures identify the contributing merge wave.
20. Record planned-vs-actual convergence evidence in this folder.
